title: The Journey That Started Something
description: I travelled all the way from Kerala to Bangalore just to prove that I could. It wasn't meant to be about love, but somehow that little ego-driven journey became the moment that set everything else in motion.

title: The Night I Told You
description: The full-night bike ride, the warmth of the night, and the moment I finally confessed my love to you.

title: Thattekad — Mini Switzerland
description: A cool morning at Thattekad. The atmosphere was calm, the grounds felt almost unreal, and we spent the morning being playful together.

title: Four Hours Close
description: Our first time cuddling. We were together for about four hours. But what stayed with me wasn't simply the closeness. My love for you was sincere. It was about you, not just the moment.

title: The First Goodbye
description: I followed your bus all the way to Perumbavoor, just to steal another twenty minutes with you. But when the time came for you to leave, I felt as though something inside me was quietly falling apart. I stood there anyway, watching you for those final few minutes, trying to hold on to the little time we had left before we had to be apart again.

title: The Day I Fell a Little Deeper
description:
Almost a month had passed since the first visit that made me fall for you, and nearly a week had gone by since you left for Bengaluru. This time, I was there to see you again.

The day was filled with little moments that, on their own, might have seemed ordinary. We sat together on a bench in front of an apartment until a man asked us to leave. We visited Cubbon Park together as a couple for the first time, shared an incredibly hot and spicy chicken fried rice for lunch, and I even fed you a few bites.

Cubbon Park gave me a little “protein” of its own, too—a memory I'll leave here in our own words. And, as usual, you entrusted me with your little belongings: your lip balm, college ID and neck chain. Before leaving, I checked all my pockets and returned your lip balm and ID, both of which we had nearly forgotten about. Your neck chain, however, remained tucked inside my shirt pocket. I didn't realise it was still there until I reached the Kodegehalli Gate bus stop.

But the moments that stayed with me most were much simpler. Whenever we crossed the busy roads, you held my hand and pulled me along beside you, looking after me in that familiar, almost instinctive way. It reminded me of how someone might guide a little brother or a child safely across the road. You may not have thought much of it, but those little gestures stayed with me throughout the day. Somewhere between one crossing and the next, I found myself falling for you a little deeper.

When it was finally time to return home, I left with a strange mixture of happiness and sadness. I was grateful for every moment we'd shared, yet already wished I could have stayed a little longer.

title: A Little Further, Just to Be With You
description:
It was the day you were returning, and for the first time, I accompanied you and your amma to say goodbye. My original plan was to part ways with you at Muvattupuzha, but I followed your bus, hoping it would stop somewhere near Perumbavoor. To my surprise, it continued right through Perumbavoor and all the way to the Indian Oil Swagath petrol pump in Angamaly.

That unexpected detour gave us a little more time together. We had ice cream, teased each other, and even had a small disagreement about Kevin. Among all these little moments, one stood out in particular: a group of schoolgirls called out “Couples corner!” from their bus. It was such an unexpected, amusing moment that it became one of the day's most vivid memories.

Before we parted, I received one last, warm hug from you. It was a small moment, but one I carried with me on the journey home.

By the time I reached Pandappilly at around 11:30 PM, my bike had travelled approximately 99 kilometres. What had begun as a simple goodbye at Muvattupuzha had turned into a much longer journey, all because I wanted a little more time with you.

title: The Two Days That Felt Like a Lifetime
description:
Day One — 10 October

It was my third visit to Bengaluru, and once again, I was there to see you. I waited at Aster Hospital until around 10:50 AM while you finished your exam. Afterwards, we walked to Theertha, hoping to have biriyani. You told me you weren't particularly hungry, but you still wanted me to eat something. I loved that little gesture; even when you didn't feel like eating yourself, you were thinking about me.

When we reached Theertha, we were told that the biriyani would only be ready by 1:30 PM. So we went upstairs for ice cream. Just as we were there, a group of your friends arrived. I was nervous, although I tried my best to stay calm. One of them even asked my name and whether I had come all the way from Kerala just to meet you. All I could manage was an awkward smile.

After our ice cream, we returned downstairs and waited for the biriyani. The chechi at the restaurant would occasionally look over at us with a gentle smile. By the time our food arrived, even the wait had become part of the memory.

We ate and headed to Sahakara Nagar Park, where we spent time sharing our music with each other. Later, we visited Vishal Mega Mart, where we accidentally broke a bag on display, and bought two packets of soan papdi and some Dairy Milk. We then spent some time at the park near Periyar Cafe before I dropped you in front of your hostel.

But the day wasn't quite over.

Around 9 PM, after you'd had dinner, I asked whether I could charge my phone inside your hostel. I handed it to you, and we talked until midnight, with the iron grill between us—you inside the hostel and me outside. Even that barrier couldn't stop us from finding a little more time together. There was another one of our private “protein” moments through the bars, and by the time we said goodnight, my phone had charged too.

Then came my first real taste of Bengaluru's nights: barking dogs, relentless mosquitoes, and very little comfort. It was hardly the peaceful night I'd imagined, but I was still excited about what the morning would bring.

Day Two — 11 October

I woke up around 3:30 AM, already excited to see you again. With so much energy and anticipation, I found myself stretching and jumping around the street while waiting for the hostel gate to open. You finally came out around 5:45 AM. During the wait, you'd given me my bag, and I changed my clothes outside the hostel—right in front of its security camera. Looking back, even that became another funny detail from our time together.

We walked towards Aster, where I brushed my teeth and freshened up before we had a good coffee. Then you suggested that we go to Madiwala for breakfast at a Kerala restaurant. We took the buses there and had appam with chicken stew. I enjoyed the meal, and seeing how much you liked it made it even better.

After breakfast, we returned to Cubbon Park and wandered around, looking for a quiet place where we could sit together. Eventually, we found somewhere to settle down and spend some time with each other.

Unfortunately, my stomach began to ache, while you were struggling with a terrible headache and leg pain. You became upset, feeling that I wasn't paying enough attention to you. I struggled to show you how much I cared because I was caught up in my own discomfort. It was a difficult moment between us, and I wished I'd been better at making you feel cared for even when I wasn't feeling well myself.

We returned to Theertha for biriyani, and by then, the people at the restaurant recognised us. After eating, we felt much more like our usual, lively selves again.

Later, we went back to Sahakara Nagar Park and sat together on a bench. That was when you began sharing your family stories with me. As you spoke about your mother, your eyes filled with tears, and I held you close while you cried. I wanted you to feel safe enough to let everything out, without having to hide what you were feeling or worry about being judged.

That moment stayed with me more deeply than anything else that day. Being trusted with your vulnerable side made me feel that I could be someone you leaned on—not someone who needed you to be happy all the time, but someone who could sit beside you when things hurt. I felt closer to you, and I found myself falling for you even more.

When we finally left the park, we bought cotton candy, and you fed me some as we walked back towards your hostel. You also gave me another familiar scolding for not eating properly. Some things, apparently, never change.

Before we parted, you gave me a warm kiss on my hand. I then began the walk to Kodegehalli Gate, carrying two days' worth of memories with me. This time, there was no need to rush. I had plenty of time before my train, so I let my thoughts wander back through everything we'd shared.

I reached KR Puram and boarded my train around 11:50 PM. The journey brought me back to Aluva at approximately 11:20 AM the following morning, and I reached home around 2:15 PM.

We took no photographs during those two days. Yet, somehow, they left me with one of the fullest collections of memories I could have asked for. From shared meals and silly accidents to sleepless nights, difficult moments, and the trust you placed in me, every part of the visit gave me something to carry home.

And with every journey I make to see you, my love for you grows a little stronger.

title: One Hour, A Thousand Feelings
description:
That day, I found myself wandering through Pandappilly town several times, hoping for a chance to see you. My repeated trips didn't go unnoticed, and they made your amma suspect that I wanted to meet you. She told you that if I wanted to come over and talk to you, I could do so when she was home.

At around 8:20 PM, amma asked whether I was coming. And just like that, I got the chance I'd been hoping for. I walked into your house, happier than I could explain, simply because I finally got to see you up close.

We talked about random things, and somehow, the arguments we'd had throughout the day no longer felt so important. Being together in person softened everything. I also got to have a conversation with your amma, which made the visit feel even more special.

Then, while your amma and brother were occupied with a phone call, I managed to steal a hug. I didn't feel like letting go. What followed was a little push-and-pull between us, and in the middle of it, I accidentally broke your phone. The most unexpected part was that your brother seemed to understand exactly what had happened.

Despite that little accident, I left the house at 9:23 PM with a heart full of happiness. From the moment I arrived to the moment I left, we had shared just over an hour together. It wasn't a long visit, but it was enough to melt away the day's arguments and leave me with another memory I wanted to keep.
